M18.intro: Assets is where you keep track of company property: laptops, phones, SIM cards, ID cards, vehicles, licences and more. You set up asset types, record each item in the asset register, hand it to employees, take it back and follow it to the end of its life.
M18.why: Without a register nobody knows who holds which laptop or phone, items go missing at exit and money for unreturned property is never recovered. PeopleOS links custody to the exit clearance and the full and final settlement.
M18.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin have full access. The Asset Admin role manages assets and, by default, fulfils asset requests and clears the Asset clearance at exit. Auditors can view the register. Managers and employees see only My assets and My asset requests.
M18.where: Organisation › Assets › Asset desk, Asset register, Asset requests, Categories, Sub types and Models. Asset settings: Admin › Setup › Setup (Asset).

procedures.title: Set up asset types, sub types and products
procedures.before: Know what kinds of property you issue, who fulfils requests for each, and which items need a signed receipt.
steps: Open Organisation › Assets › Categories. Eleven starter types are ready. Edit a type and set Status to Inactive if you never use it.
Edit a type: turn on Serial number required where needed, enter Useful life in months, choose the Role and the Due days.
Click New asset category, enter Name and Code, and save. The code cannot be changed later.
Open Sub types and click Add asset sub type. Choose the Asset type, name it and decide on duplicate serials and acknowledgement.
Open Models and click New asset model. Choose Category, enter Manufacturer and Model, Product life, Specifications and attach documents.
procedures.result: Your asset types, sub types and products are ready to use on the register and on requests.

procedures.title: Receive a new asset into stock
procedures.before: The asset type (and product) exists. Have the tag, serial number and invoice at hand.
steps: Go to Organisation › Assets › Asset register and click Receive asset.
Choose Category, then Sub type and Model. Enter Asset tag, Name, Serial number, Condition, Owned by and Location. Click Next.
Enter Purchase date, Purchase cost, Vendor, Invoice number and Warranty until. Click Next.
Check the details and click Create asset.
procedures.result: The asset is In stock, its Lifecycle shows Procured, and its page is open ready for Assign.

procedures.title: Assign an asset to an employee
procedures.before: The asset is In stock and the employee is a current employee.
steps: In Asset register, click View on an In stock asset.
Choose the Employee, the date, the Condition at handover and, if it must come back, Expected return on. Add a note.
Submit. The status becomes Assigned and the employee becomes the custodian.
If the sub type needs it, the employee gets a task and reminders until they acknowledge. Watch Waiting for acknowledgement.
procedures.result: The asset shows the custodian, Custody history has an active row and the employee's timeline records the handover.

procedures.title: Transfer an asset or take it back
procedures.before: The asset is Assigned.
steps: Click View on the asset in the Asset register.
Click Transfer, choose the New custodian, add a note and submit. The old custody closes and a new one opens.
Click Take back, choose the Condition on return (Good by default), add a note and submit.
Open Custody history and Lifecycle to see the change.
procedures.result: After a transfer the new employee holds the asset; after Take back it is In stock with no custodian.

procedures.title: Send an asset for repair and bring it back
procedures.before: The asset is In stock or Assigned.
steps: On the asset page open More › Send for repair. Describe the Issue and the Vendor.
An assigned asset is first taken back as Not working. The status becomes In repair and a repair row opens.
When it returns, open More › Back from repair. Enter Cost, Condition and Resolution.
The asset is In stock. Use Assign if the employee should get it back.
procedures.result: The Repairs tab shows the visit with cost and resolution, and the asset is back in stock.

procedures.title: Report a loss, retire or dispose of an asset
procedures.before: Decide whether the item is lost, no longer used, or leaving the company.
steps: More › Report lost, confirm and give a note. Any custody closes; status becomes Lost. Use Found if it turns up.
For an asset In stock, In repair or Lost: More › Retire with a reason. It stays in the register as Retired.
More › Dispose: choose Method (Sale, Scrap, Donation, Returned to vendor, Write-off), date, Realised value and reference.
Lifecycle shows the step. A disposed asset has no further actions.
procedures.result: The asset's final state is recorded with a reason and an audit entry.
procedures.source: AssetActions.php (lost, found, retire, dispose); Assets::markLost, retire, dispose

procedures.title: Raise and fulfil an asset request for an employee
procedures.before: The asset type is active. For a new asset, a matching asset is in stock.
steps: Open Asset requests and click Request for an employee. Choose Employee, Request for, the Asset type or Asset, Reason and Needed by.
If it shows Waiting for approval, the line manager or asset team uses Approve (or the workflow, if one is set).
When it shows To fulfil, click Fulfil. Choose the Asset to hand over (for a return: the condition) and add a note.
Use Decline with a reason if it cannot be met, or Cancel if it is no longer needed.
procedures.result: The request is Fulfilled and the asset is assigned, replaced or taken back on the employee's record.

procedures.title: Choose asset settings and the asset entitlement policy
procedures.before: Agree with HR and IT who approves requests and how unreturned assets are recovered.
steps: On the Asset desk open Asset setup › Setup centre: asset (Admin › Setup › Setup, Asset).
Set Which asset requests follow a workflow, and who may choose the sub type and the product in requests.
Set the days to hand over joiners' entitled assets and the reminder interval for acknowledgements.
Decide whether assets must be recovered, how the amount is suggested, return requests, exceptions and collection days.
In Workflows › Policies add an Asset entitlement policy: the assets each group gets, what they may request, and HR limits.
procedures.result: Requests, joiner hand-overs, reminders and exit recovery follow your organisation's rules.

procedures.title: Recover assets when an employee leaves
procedures.before: An exit case has been initiated for the employee (People › Lifecycle › Exit cases).
steps: With the default settings, a Return request is raised for each asset the employee holds, Raised by Exit, due by the last working day.
Fulfil each return request, or use Take back on the asset page, recording the condition.
In People › Lifecycle › Clearances, open the Asset clearance and click Clear. Tick each Return item.
Enter Amount to recover in F&F (book value may be suggested), or, if your settings allow, a waiver reason.
The amounts appear as an Asset recovery deduction in the full and final settlement.
procedures.result: All company property is back or its value is recovered, and the asset clearance is cleared.

procedures.title: Check the Asset desk
steps: Go to Organisation › Assets › Asset desk.
Each tile shows a register with something in it and its count. Click a tile to open that view.
Use Asset acknowledgement for unsigned hand-overs and Asset request for open requests.
Open Reports › Report library for ready-made asset reports.
procedures.result: You know what is in stock, in repair, lost, waiting for acknowledgement and waiting to be fulfilled.

calculations.title: Book value of an asset (suggested recovery at exit)
calculations.intro: PeopleOS works out book value by straight-line depreciation over the product life (else the asset type's useful life). The cost and date are from the example organisation; the 36-month life is illustrative, because the example sets no life.
explain: Cost × (life − full months since purchase) ÷ life, rounded to 2 decimals, never below 0.
No life or no purchase date
Book value equals the purchase cost. No cost: 0.
As the suggested Amount to recover in F&F on the Asset clearance, when the setting suggests Book value.
Amount suggested for unreturned assets is Entered by hand: no amount is suggested.

calculations.title: Due date of a joiner's entitled asset
calculations.intro: Under an asset entitlement policy, each entitled asset is raised as a request when the employee joins. The joining date here is illustrative; 7 days is the default setting in the example organisation.

explain: Due on = the approval date (or the raising date, if no approval is needed) + the asset type's Due days.
Due on = last working day − collection days (0 by default), never earlier than today.

warnings.title: Status changes only through the asset's actions
warnings.headline: Edit cannot change an asset's status or custodian.
warnings.body: Assign, Transfer, Take back, repair, lost, retire and dispose are buttons on the asset page. Each one adds a Lifecycle line and audit entry, so history stays complete.
points: Use Take back before you dispose of or retire an assigned asset.
Use Change location, not Edit, when you want the move recorded in Lifecycle.
warnings.todo: Train asset staff to act from the asset page, never by editing details.

warnings.title: Assets still held block the exit
warnings.headline: The Asset clearance will not clear while the employee holds company assets.
warnings.body: With the default setting, you must take every asset back or enter an amount to recover. If your organisation allows waivers, a written reason is needed and is audited.
points: The clearance message names the asset tags still held.
The amount flows into the full and final settlement as Asset recovery.
warnings.todo: Fulfil the exit return requests before the last working day.

warnings.title: Codes and tags are permanent
warnings.headline: Asset type codes, sub type codes and asset tags cannot be changed after creation, and records cannot be deleted.
warnings.body: Uploads and reports use these codes and tags. Choose a naming scheme before you load data. To stop using a type, sub type or product, set it to Inactive.
points: Asset tags are saved in capitals and must be unique in your organisation.
warnings.todo: Agree the tag format (for example LT-0001) with IT before receiving assets.

warnings.title: Disposal is final
warnings.headline: A disposed asset has no further actions.
warnings.body: Dispose only works when the asset is not assigned. After disposal it stays in the register for history but cannot be assigned, repaired or reported found.
points: Retired assets can still be disposed of later.
A lost asset can be marked Found until it is retired or disposed of.
warnings.todo: Check the method, date and realised value before you confirm.

warnings.title: Entitlement policy can refuse HR assignments
warnings.headline: Under an asset policy set to 'No, only the mapped assets', assignments outside the policy are refused.
warnings.body: The setting applies to HR too. 'Yes, with a warning' allows the assignment but records it in the audit trail. Without an asset policy, any asset can be assigned.
points: Employees may also be limited to requesting only mapped assets.
warnings.todo: Review the policy before switching it to mapped-only.

M19.intro: Workforce planning describes your organisation's capacity: positions with seats and FTE, the hierarchy between them, open seats, and the headcount plans, scenarios and budgets that say how capacity should change. It also holds the customers and projects your people work on.
M19.why: Without positions and plans you cannot see approved capacity against the people you actually have, or which seats are empty. Plans and budgets kept outside PeopleOS drift from the real organisation and cannot be compared with payroll cost.
M19.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold every workforce and project permission. Executives see only Workforce overview and Workforce analytics. Auditors read positions, plans, customers and projects. Managers see only the positions under them, never plans or costs.
M19.where: Organisation › Workforce: Workforce overview, Positions, Position hierarchy, Vacancies, Scenarios, Headcount plans, Headcount budgets, Workforce snapshots, Workforce analytics, Customers, Projects.
objectives: Create a position and take it from draft through approval to open, then fill and change it from an effective date.
Prepare a scenario, a headcount plan and a budget, get each approved by a second person and read the forecast and comparisons.
Read capacity, occupancy and vacancies today or on any past date, and keep customers and projects with their members up to date.
depends_on: M03 Organisation structure: companies, organisation units and locations give each position, plan and budget its place
M04 Masters and configuration: designations, job families, grades, employment types and cost centres fill the position definition
M07 Employees: an employee occupies a seat through Transfer / promote on their profile (or the Position step when hiring)
M13 Payroll: finalised payroll employer cost is the actual cost compared with an employer-cost budget
M09 Exit: exits recorded with a last working day reduce occupied seats in a plan's forecast
M05 Users and access: a second user with approval rights is needed, because nobody approves their own submission

organisation/workforce-overview.purpose: The landing page of Workforce: eight tiles that show approved, occupied and vacant seats, employees, planned and frozen seats, items waiting for a decision and active plans, all as of today.

organisation/workforce-overview.limits: Shows today only. To see an earlier date use Workforce snapshots.

The date the position first takes effect.

procedures.title: Create a position as a draft
procedures.before: The company or organisation unit, designation, grade and location exist (Organisation structure and masters).
steps: Go to Organisation › Workforce › Positions and click New position.
Enter a unique Code (e.g. ENG-BE-01) and the Effective from date the position starts.
Choose Designation (job / role); Title, Job family and Grade fill from it when left empty.
Choose Organisation unit (or Company), Location, Cost centre and, if it reports to another position, Parent position.
Choose Occupancy mode. For Multiple occupants enter Seats and FTE per seat; FTE capacity defaults to seats × FTE.
Add a Reason and confirm. The message 'Position … created as a draft' appears.
procedures.result: A Draft position (version 1). It is not yet capacity and cannot be occupied.

procedures.title: Take a position from draft to open
procedures.before: A draft position, and a second user with approval rights (you cannot approve your own proposal).
steps: Open the position with View. Use Edit draft to correct anything; a draft is changed in place.
Click Lifecycle › Propose. Leave Effective from empty for today. Status becomes Proposed.
Another approver opens the position and clicks Lifecycle › Approve. Status becomes Approved.
Click Lifecycle › Mark planned if the seat opens later, or Lifecycle › Open when it can be filled now.
The position now counts in Approved seats on Workforce overview; an Open one with an empty seat appears on Vacancies.
procedures.result: An Open position whose seats can be occupied by employees.

procedures.title: Put an employee in a seat, or vacate it
procedures.before: An Open position with a free seat and enough FTE capacity.
steps: Go to People › Lifecycle › Employees and open the employee's profile.
Click Transfer / promote. In Context choose the change type and Effective from.
In Change pick Position (seat); only Open positions are listed. Enter FTE if the person works less than a full seat.
To leave a seat without taking another, switch on Vacate current position instead.
Check Before → After in Review, enter the reason and click Confirm change.
procedures.result: The employee occupies the seat from that date; OCCUPIED on Positions and Vacancies update. For new joiners, choose the seat in the Position step of the hire wizard.

procedures.title: Change a position from a date and decide the change request
procedures.before: A position that is not Draft, Abolished or Closed.
steps: Open it from Positions and click Change from a date.
Set Effective from (not before the latest version), fill only the changed fields and give a Reason.
Location, title, designation and cost centre changes apply at once as a new version. Seats, FTE, unit, parent or grade changes become a change request.
Another approver opens the Change requests tab and clicks Approve, or Reject with a note. The requester can Cancel.
The History tab lists every version with its dates, seats, FTE, parent and reason.
procedures.result: A new effective-dated version; the previous version ends the day before. Nothing is overwritten.

procedures.title: Freeze, hold, abolish or close a position
procedures.before: For Abolish and Close, nobody occupies the position from the chosen date.
steps: Open it from Positions and click Lifecycle.
Freeze or Put on hold stops new assignments; Unfreeze reopens a frozen one; Abolish or Close ends it.
A reason is required for Freeze, Put on hold, Abolish, Close and for unfreezing.
Abolish and Close ask for confirmation; they are final.
procedures.result: The position moves to the new status from the chosen date. Frozen and on-hold seats are no longer vacancies.

procedures.title: Prepare a scenario and have it approved
procedures.before: Agree the planning assumptions with finance or leadership.
steps: Open Scenarios and click New scenario.
Enter Code, Name and Description, e.g. GROWTH-27 · Growth 2027.
Enter Expected attrition % per year (0–100), Expected growth % and Other assumptions.
Another approver clicks Approve on the row. The scenario is then locked.
procedures.result: An approved scenario that plans can use; its attrition % drives the plan forecast.

procedures.title: Build, approve and publish a headcount plan
procedures.before: A company or unit to plan for; optionally a scenario. A different person must review and approve.
steps: Open Headcount plans, click New plan, enter Code, Name, Company or Organisation unit, Scenario, Period type and dates.
On the draft row open Actions › Add line. Choose Movement, Headcount, FTE and an Effective date inside the period.
Use Lines and Forecast to check net headcount and the month-by-month view.
Actions › Submit. The version is locked and becomes Submitted; it needs at least one line.
Another person uses Start review, then Approve. They can also Reject or Return for changes with a note.
An approver uses Publish (make active). Any earlier active version becomes Superseded.
procedures.result: An Active plan version, shown under PLANNED VS ACTUAL on Workforce analytics. Live positions are not changed.

procedures.title: Correct a plan or turn a plan line into a position
procedures.before: An Approved or Active plan version.
steps: Actions › New version (correction) copies the lines into a new draft version; change it and submit again.
A plan can have one draft version at a time; finish or archive it before starting another.
Actions › Propose position from line. Pick a New position or Position expansion line and enter a Position code.
The new position is Proposed; a second person approves it on Positions before it can open.
procedures.result: A corrected plan version, or a proposed position linked to its plan line.

procedures.title: Record a budget and compare it with plan and payroll
procedures.before: You hold workforce.costs. For actual cost, payroll for the period is finalised.
steps: Open Headcount budgets and click New budget.
Enter Name, Company or Organisation unit, optional Cost centre, Period start and Period end.
Choose Cost basis (Employer cost to compare with payroll), Amount and Currency. Optionally pick a Plan version.
Another approver clicks Approve on the row.
Click Planned vs actual to see budget, planned, actual and the two differences.
procedures.result: An approved budget; while it covers today it also appears under BUDGET VS ACTUAL on Workforce analytics.

procedures.title: Add a customer and a project with members
procedures.before: The employees who will work on the project are current or joining employees.
steps: Open Customers, click New customer, fill Name, Code and contact, then Create customer.
Open Projects, click New project, choose the Customer, Company, Status and Billable, then dates and Manager.
Check Review and click Create project.
Open the project with Edit, go to Members and click Add member: Employee, Role, Allocation (%), From, To.
Use Take off on the member row and enter the Last day on the project.
procedures.result: A project with its customer and members. In the example organisation, Northwind store app (PRJ-NW-APP) has 3 members.

procedures.title: Compare the workforce today with a past date
procedures.before: Positions and assignments carry correct effective dates.
steps: Go to Organisation › Workforce › Workforce snapshots. The tiles show today.
Choose a date in As of; the tiles and tables recalculate for that day.
Compare BY DEPARTMENT and BY LOCATION with today's figures.
If needed, choose the same date in As of on Position hierarchy.
procedures.result: A reconstruction of capacity and headcount on the chosen date.

calculations.title: FTE capacity of a position
calculations.intro: When you do not enter FTE capacity, PeopleOS sets it to seats × FTE per seat, rounded to two decimals. Illustrative numbers.
explain: FTE capacity = Seats × FTE per seat. A Single occupant position always has 1 seat.
FTE column on Positions; FTE capacity on the position's Overview.

calculations.title: Vacant seats
calculations.intro: Vacant seats are counted only in Open positions: seats minus occupied seats, never below zero. Frozen empty seats are not vacancies. Illustrative numbers.
lines: Frozen position C: 2 seats − 0 occupied (not counted)
explain: Vacant = sum over Open positions of (seats − occupied seats). Position C shows under Frozen seats (2).
Vacant seats on Workforce overview and Workforce snapshots; VACANT on Vacancies.

calculations.title: Net headcount of a plan version
calculations.intro: Each plan line adds or removes seats according to its movement. Illustrative numbers.
explain: Existing capacity (baseline), New position, Position expansion, Transfer in.
Position reduction, Position closure, Transfer out, Retirement, Known exit.
NET HEADCOUNT on Headcount plans; PLANNED NET CHANGE on Workforce analytics.

calculations.title: Budget compared with planned and actual cost
calculations.intro: Planned vs actual subtracts each figure from the budget. Actual cost is shown only for an Employer cost budget in the payroll currency covering at least 5 employees. Illustrative numbers.
lines: Planned cost from plan lines on the same basis
explain: Budget − actual finalised payroll employer cost, e.g. 12,000,000.00 − 5,400,000.00 = 6,600,000.00.
Sum of costed plan lines on the budget's basis, signed by movement.
Planned vs actual on Headcount budgets; BUDGET VS ACTUAL on Workforce analytics.

calculations.title: Assumed attrition in the plan forecast
calculations.intro: If the plan's scenario has an attrition %, the forecast shows a monthly assumption based on seats occupied at the start. It is labelled an assumption, never a prediction about anyone. Illustrative numbers.
explain: Occupied at start × attrition % ÷ 12, rounded to one decimal; added up month after month.
Approved seats at start plus each month's planned change from the lines.
Exits with a last working day in the month reduce occupied seats.

warnings.title: A second person approves
warnings.headline: Nobody approves or decides their own submission.
warnings.body: Approving a position, deciding a position change, reviewing or approving a plan version, and approving a scenario or budget must be done by someone other than the person who prepared it.
points: The approve buttons are hidden for the person who submitted.
The approver needs workforce.approve (and workforce.costs for budgets).
warnings.todo: Give a second administrator or HR lead an approving role before you start planning.

warnings.title: Positions are capacity, not people
warnings.headline: Workforce never moves, promotes or removes anyone.
warnings.body: Occupied is worked out from employee assignments. Abolishing or closing an occupied position, or cutting seats below current occupancy, is refused.
points: Vacate or move the occupant first through Transfer / promote.
A transfer that does not name a position keeps the employee's seat.
warnings.todo: Before abolishing or shrinking a position, check its Occupancy tab.

warnings.title: Dates cannot go back
warnings.headline: A change cannot start before the position's latest version.
warnings.body: Every change after draft is a new version from an effective date; the previous version ends the day before. Versions are never edited or deleted.
points: To correct the past, record a later version or create a new position.
A position always keeps its company.
warnings.todo: Choose effective dates carefully, especially when back-dating.

warnings.title: Plans do not change live positions
warnings.headline: Approving or publishing a plan creates no positions.
warnings.body: A plan states intended capacity only. The single bridge is Propose position from line, which creates a Proposed position that still needs approval.
points: Only New position and Position expansion lines can propose a position.
Each line proposes at most one position.
warnings.todo: After publishing a plan, propose and approve the positions it needs.

warnings.title: Actual cost is shown only when comparable
warnings.headline: Actual cost appears only for an Employer cost budget in the same currency.
warnings.body: Actual cost comes from finalised payroll employer cost. Other bases, another currency, or fewer than 5 employees show a note instead of a figure, so no individual pay is revealed.
points: Budget amounts and costs are visible only with workforce.costs.
warnings.todo: Use the Employer cost basis for budgets you want to compare with payroll.

warnings.title: Vacancies are not recruitment
warnings.headline: PeopleOS has no job requisitions or recruitment.
warnings.body: A vacancy is unfilled capacity in an open position. Hiring happens outside PeopleOS; an integration can be told when a position opens or is vacated.
warnings.todo: Use Vacancies as the list of seats to fill, and hire through your usual process.

You proposed or submitted it yourself, or you lack workforce.approve
Ask another approver to approve it

Choose that date or later

Vacate or move them with Transfer / promote, then abolish or close
'The new capacity is below the current occupancy'

Vacate seats first or keep the capacity
The position is not in the Position (seat) list on Transfer / promote
Only Open positions are listed
Open the position first (Lifecycle › Open)

All seats or FTE are taken from that date
Vacate a seat, add seats with Change from a date, or choose another position
'A plan version needs at least one line before it is submitted'
The draft has no lines
Add at least one line with Actions › Add line
'A plan line's effective date falls inside the planning period'
The line date is outside the plan's period
Enter a date between Period start and Period end
Planned vs actual shows '—' for actual with a note
Basis is not Employer cost, currency differs, or fewer than 5 employees
Read the note; use an Employer cost budget in the payroll currency

Set the customer Inactive / choose a current employee
checklist: Masters ready
Companies, units, locations, designations, grades and cost centres exist.
Second approver
At least one other user holds workforce.approve (and workforce.costs for budgets).
Positions created
Each position has a code, designation, unit, location and correct seats and FTE.
Positions approved and open

Seats filled

Hierarchy checked
Parent positions set; Position hierarchy shows the expected tree.
Vacancies reviewed
Vacancies list matches the seats you intend to fill.
Scenario approved
Planning assumptions recorded and approved before the plan uses them.
Plan active
Plan lines dated inside the period, approved and published.
Budget approved
Employer cost basis for payroll comparison; approved by a second person.
Customers and projects
Customers, projects, managers and members up to date; finished projects Completed.
Monthly look
Workforce overview and Workforce analytics checked; decisions waiting cleared.
summary: A position is capacity (seats and FTE); employees occupy it through their employment record.
Positions move Draft → Proposed → Approved → Planned/Open, and can be frozen, put on hold, abolished or closed.
Every later change is a dated version; some changes become change requests for a second person.
Plans, scenarios and budgets are prepared by one person and approved by another; plans never change live positions.
Vacancies are empty seats in open positions, not recruitment requisitions.
Costs are visible only with workforce.costs; actual cost comes from finalised payroll employer cost.

M20.intro: The Services area gives employees one front door to HR: requests and questions worked against service levels, a confidential channel for grievances, and a knowledge base of policies they read and acknowledge. You set up categories, SLAs, the catalogue and routing, and oversee the queues.
M20.why: Without categories, approved services and routing, requests land with nobody and service levels are not measured. Without handler roles, confidential grievances may reach the wrong people; without acknowledgements you cannot show employees were informed.
M20.who: You (Tenant Super Admin), the Tenant HR Admin and the HR Manager hold every service desk, grievance and knowledge permission. Auditors can read the HR queue and articles. Managers and employees raise requests and grievances and read articles; managers also see their team's request status.
M20.where: Services › Service Desk (HR queue, Service catalogue, Resolver rules, SLA policies, Categories & SLAs, Service analytics); Services › Grievances (Cases, Categories & handlers); Services › Knowledge (Articles). Settings: Admin › Setup › Helpdesk and Admin › Setup › Engage.
objectives: Set up request categories, SLA policies, catalogue services and resolver rules so every request reaches the right team with a measured due time.
Work and supervise the HR queue: assign, reply, pause, resolve, close, reopen, escalate and protect confidential cases.
Configure grievance handling and publish knowledge articles that employees read and acknowledge, and track who did.
depends_on: M05 Users, access and integrations: agents need servicedesk.agent; teams, escalation and grievance handlers are roles; data access groups set each agent's scope
M10 Attendance and time office: the employee's holiday calendar and work-location timezone drive business-hours SLAs
M06 Workflows and policies: approval workflows for services, and the Helpdesk access policy that limits what employee groups may raise
M04 Masters and configuration: Admin › Setup › Helpdesk and Engage hold the helpdesk and HR handbook settings
M21 Communication and engagement: notification rules and templates decide how request, grievance and article notices are sent

services/categories-and-slas.purpose: The request categories employees pick when they ask HR something, each with its resolution and first-response hours, default agent or team, escalation role and closing rules.
services/categories-and-slas.when: At set-up, and whenever you add a kind of request or change who handles it or how fast.

Resolution and first-response hours. They apply when no SLA policy covers the request (calendar hours).
Who gets new requests of this category when no resolver rule or service routing applies.
A workflow started automatically with each request of this category, for example a letter approval flow.
Catalogue services filed under this category.
Whether a root cause is mandatory at resolution, and whether the employee is asked to rate the help.
Changes a category; the code cannot be changed after creation. Add a Reason for change for the audit trail.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: What employees see in "What is it about?".

fields.label: Code

fields.label: Sort order

fields.label: Status

When to warn, whom to escalate to, how often and how far, and which statuses stop the clock.
Days resolvers work and their hours (business calendar only).
First response and resolution hours, or due days, for each priority.

procedures.title: Set up a request category
procedures.before: Roles for your HR teams and for escalation exist, with servicedesk.agent for agents.
steps: Go to Services › Service Desk › Categories & SLAs and click New ticket category (or Edit on an existing one).
Enter Name, Code and Sort order, keep Status Active and choose the Purpose (General for most).
Enter Resolution SLA and First response in hours, and choose Escalate breaches to role.
Choose a Default agent or a role in "or agents with role". Optionally pick a workflow in Start workflow.
Decide if helpdesk RCA is mandatory and whether the employee rates the help, then save.
procedures.result: Employees and agents can choose the category in Ask HR; new requests go to its agent or team.

procedures.title: Create an SLA policy with business hours
procedures.before: Holiday calendars and work locations are set up for your employees.
steps: Go to Services › Service Desk › SLA policies and click New SLA policy.
Enter Name and Code, choose Calendar "Business hours", set Effective from and Status Active.
Set the warning share (e.g. 75), Escalate to (role), Escalate again every (hours), Highest escalation level and pause statuses.
Tick the days resolvers work and set Start time and End time (blank = Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00).
For Low, Normal, High and Urgent enter First response and Resolution hours, or type due days to fill the hours.
Check the Review step and create the policy.
procedures.result: An active policy you can attach to service versions and resolver rules.

procedures.title: Release a catalogue service (draft to active)
procedures.before: The service exists (starter services are already there as drafts). For approval, an active published workflow exists. A second person can approve.
steps: Go to Services › Service Desk › Service catalogue and click Open on the service.
On the Versions tab open the version actions and choose Edit draft.
Set Effective from, default priority, description, request form, hand-off, attachment rule and confidentiality.
Tick Available to (employees, managers, HR), Shown in the catalogue, visibility switches and any company, department or location limits.
Switch on approval and choose the workflow if needed, pick the SLA policy and the Team (role). Save the draft.
Choose Submit for approval and confirm. The version is frozen.
A different person with approval rights opens it and chooses Approve (or Return to draft with a note).
procedures.result: The version is Active (or scheduled for its date) and the service appears to the chosen audiences.

procedures.title: Add a new service and change a live one
procedures.before: Its category exists.
steps: In Service catalogue click New service, enter Name, Code, Category, optional Subcategory and Sort order, then create.
The service opens with draft version 1: complete it, submit it and have it approved as above.
Open the service, click New version on the Versions tab and pick the date the change starts.
Edit the new draft (it copies the latest version), submit it and have it approved.
On its date the new version becomes Active and the old one Superseded; open requests keep their version.
procedures.result: The catalogue changes from a known date without affecting requests already raised.

procedures.title: Route requests with a resolver rule
procedures.before: The team role exists and its members hold servicedesk.agent with the right data access scope.
steps: Go to Services › Service Desk › Resolver rules and click Add rule.
Enter Rule name and Priority, choose categories, services, companies and locations (empty = any).
Choose Assigned to (role), optionally a Default resolver and a role to intimate.
Choose an SLA policy (or leave blank for the service or category SLA), Status and dates.
Check and create. The review page shows days off, working hours and due times per priority.
procedures.result: Matching new requests go to the rule's team with the rule's SLA.

procedures.title: Raise a request for an employee
procedures.before: The employee is in your data access scope and the category is active.
steps: In Services › Service Desk › HR queue click Ask HR.
Pick For employee; the employee's header is shown.
Choose What is it about?, enter Subject and Description and set Priority.
The "Who approves this" section shows who handles it.
Submit. A message shows the request number with a link to follow it.
procedures.result: A request (TKT-…) raised by HR, with its due times set and its team or agent assigned.

procedures.title: Work a request to resolution
procedures.before: You hold servicedesk.agent and the employee is in your scope.
steps: In HR queue use Unassigned or SLA at risk, click Open, then Acknowledge and Take it (or More › Assign to someone).
Click Reply; choose "Visible to the employee" or "Internal HR note", add a file if needed.
Wait for employee pauses the SLA until the employee replies; Wait for HR records an internal hold. (Actions not shown as buttons are under More.)
For data-change services, Apply the change runs it once; it cannot be done by the person who requested or approved it.
Choose Resolve: write the resolution, add the root cause if required and optionally link a knowledge article.
procedures.result: The request is Resolved; the employee is told and can close and rate it. It closes automatically after 5 days.

procedures.title: Close, reopen or cancel a request
procedures.before: You can work the request.
steps: On a Resolved request choose Close. The employee closes with "Close & rate" instead.
On a Resolved or Closed request choose More › Reopen and give a reason. The resolution clock restarts in full.
On an open request choose More › Cancel request, confirm and give a reason.
Open the Status history tab to see each move, who made it and why.
procedures.result: The request is closed, back in progress with a new due time, or cancelled, all audited.

procedures.title: Act on several requests at once
procedures.before: You hold servicedesk.bulk.
steps: In HR queue tick the requests (up to 500).
Open the bulk menu: Assign, Move status or Escalate.
Assign needs an Agent; Move status allows Acknowledged, In progress, Waiting for employee or Waiting for HR; Escalate needs a reason.
A message lists how many were updated and why any were skipped or refused, with an operation id.
procedures.result: Each request is checked and changed on its own; nothing fails silently.

procedures.title: Set up grievance categories and handlers
procedures.before: Handler roles exist (for example an Internal Committee role) and their members hold grievance.view or grievance.manage.
steps: Go to Services › Grievances › Categories & handlers and click Edit on a category (or New grievance category).
Set Resolve within (days), Confidential (handlers only) and Allow anonymous cases.
Choose Handled by roles, e.g. the Internal Committee for PoSH.
Add a Reason for change and save.
procedures.result: New cases of the category go to the least-loaded handler and are visible to handlers only (if confidential).

procedures.title: Handle a grievance case
procedures.before: You are the handler, hold a handler role, or have grievance.manage on a category without handler roles.
steps: Go to Services › Grievances › Cases and click Open.
If unassigned, click Assign and choose the Handler.
Use Update status (Under review, Investigating, Action taken) and Add to case file for notes, evidence, actions and decisions.
Tick Visible to the employee only on entries the complainant should read; use More › Grant access with a reason if a colleague must help.
Choose Resolve (under More) and write the resolution, then Close case and confirm.
procedures.result: A complete, audited case file and a closed case.

procedures.title: Publish a policy that employees must acknowledge
procedures.before: A second person holds kb.review to review your article.
steps: Go to Services › Knowledge › Articles and click New article. Fill Title, Category, Summary and Body.
Switch on Employees must acknowledge and, if needed, Mandatory reading; add audience conditions or leave empty for everyone.
Review and create. The article is a Draft.
Click Submit for review on its row. A reviewer (not you) approves or returns it with a note.
When the status is Approved, click Publish. Version 1 is created and the audience is asked to acknowledge.
procedures.result: A published, numbered version that employees read and acknowledge.

procedures.title: Track acknowledgements and revise a policy
procedures.before: The article is published with acknowledgement required.
steps: In Articles read the READ / ACK column, then click Who acknowledged on the row.
Click Acknowledgements (CSV) for code, name, department, designation, read and acknowledged times and source.
Click Start a revision. Readers keep the published version; edit the draft with a Reason for change.
Submit for review, have it approved, and Publish. Everyone in the audience must acknowledge the new version.
procedures.result: A record of who acknowledged which version, and an updated policy.

calculations.title: Due time from category hours (no SLA policy)
calculations.intro: When no SLA policy applies, the category hours are used in calendar hours, adjusted by priority. Figures from the example organisation (request TKT-2026-00001).
lines: Letters & certificates: 72 h ÷ 2 for High priority
explain: Urgent = ¼ of the hours (at least 4), High = ½ (at least 8), Normal = the hours, Low = twice the hours.
HR queue › request › Assignment and SLA (First response due, Resolution due).
calculations.source: app/Domain/ServiceDesk/Services/SlaClock.php (legacyHours); q.php SELECT on tickets and ticket_categories

calculations.title: Due time in business hours
calculations.intro: With a business-hours SLA policy the clock runs only on service days within working hours. Illustrative: Standard HR service, Normal priority (18 h), default Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00, raised Monday 15:00.
total: Resolution target used up: due Wednesday 15:00
explain: Public and company holidays on the employee's holiday calendar are skipped; a half-day holiday counts its first half only.
Taken from the employee's work location.
Normal = 4 h: 3 h on Monday + 1 h on Tuesday = due Tuesday 10:00.
While paused (e.g. Waiting for employee) the clock stops; on resuming, both due times move later by the paused service time.

calculations.title: Due days converted to resolution hours
calculations.intro: On the Targets per priority step, typing due days fills Resolution (hours). Illustrative, with the default working day.
explain: A calendar-hours policy counts 24 h per day, so 2 due days = 48 h.
If the policy sets its own Start time and End time, that day length is used instead.

calculations.title: Escalation level of a breached request
calculations.intro: An hourly run raises the escalation level of open, unpaused requests past their due time. Illustrative: 25 hours past due, Escalate again every 24 hours, highest level 3.
lines: Whole repeat periods passed (25 h ÷ 24 h, rounded down)
explain: Level = 1 + whole hours past due ÷ repeat hours, never above Highest escalation level.
Clock hours since the due time, not service hours.
Members of the SLA policy's escalation role (else the category's) who can see the request, plus the agent.

calculations.title: SLA compliance on Service analytics
calculations.intro: SLA compliance is the share of resolved requests (with a due time) resolved on or before their due time, excluding restricted cases. Illustrative figures.
lines: Resolved on or before the due time
Resolved requests with a due time
explain: Hours from submission to resolution less paused time, averaged over resolved requests.
No figures at all if fewer than 5 employees raised requests in the period.

warnings.title: Starter services are drafts
warnings.headline: No catalogue service is available until a second person approves it.
warnings.body: PeopleOS provides starter services (salary certificate, address change, bank account change and others) as Draft version 1. In the example organisation all 13 show Not available.
points: Complete each draft: SLA policy, team, confidentiality, approval workflow.
The approver must be a different person with servicedesk.catalogue_approve.
Until then employees can still use Ask HR in a request category.
warnings.todo: Plan who prepares and who approves, then release the services you want to offer.

warnings.title: Restricted cases are hidden, even from you
warnings.headline: A restricted request is seen only by its agent, its case owner and people granted access.
warnings.body: Holding every permission is not enough. Restricted (confidential or employee-relations) services keep cases out of the general queue and analytics shows them only as a total.
points: Grant access with a reason from the case (More › Grant access); it is audited.
Granted access cannot be withdrawn from the screen today.
Opening a sensitive or restricted case is recorded in the audit trail.
warnings.todo: Use Restricted only for services that truly need it and give servicedesk.confidential to a small group.

warnings.title: Handler roles change who sees confidential grievances
warnings.headline: Once a confidential category has handler roles, grievance managers outside those roles no longer see its cases.
warnings.body: Cases are visible to the assigned handler, people granted access, members of the handler roles and the named complainant. Grievance managers see confidential cases only while a category has no handler roles.
points: In the example organisation no category has handlers, so new cases are unassigned.
Make sure at least one active person holds each handler role.
Anonymous cases never show who raised them, even in the audit trail.
warnings.todo: Set handler roles for every confidential category, PoSH first.

warnings.title: SLA policies in use are locked
warnings.headline: You cannot change the targets, hours or escalation of a policy used by an approved service version.
warnings.body: Requests take their due times from the policy when raised. To change a service level, create a new policy from a later date and attach it in a new service version.
points: Name and Status can still be changed.
Open requests keep the due times they started with.
warnings.todo: Name policies clearly (e.g. with the year) so new versions are easy to tell apart.

warnings.title: No escalation role set
warnings.headline: Breached requests are only told to the agent until an escalation role is set.
warnings.body: In the example organisation neither the Standard HR service policy nor the categories name an escalation role. Breaches still raise the escalation level, but no supervisor is told.
points: Set Escalate to (role) on SLA policies.
Set Escalate breaches to role on categories for requests without a policy.
warnings.todo: Choose an HR lead role for escalations before going live.

warnings.title: Each version needs a new acknowledgement
warnings.headline: Publishing a revision asks everyone in the audience to acknowledge again.
warnings.body: Acknowledgements are kept per version: an acknowledgement of version 1 does not count for version 2. The history is kept.
points: Avoid publishing small wording fixes of acknowledged policies.
Weekly reminders go to people who have not acknowledged.
warnings.todo: Group changes into one revision and tell employees why they must acknowledge again.

troubleshooting: Version in force shows "Not available"
The service has no approved version in force today (draft, pending, or scheduled for a later date).
Submit the draft and have a second person approve it; scheduled versions become Active on their date.
Approve is missing on a pending version
You prepared that version, or you lack servicedesk.catalogue_approve.
Ask another person with approval rights to approve it.
Submit refused: "A service that needs approval needs an active, published approval workflow."
Approval is switched on but the chosen workflow is not active and published.
Publish the workflow in Workflows, or switch off approval in the draft.
"This SLA policy is used by an approved service version; create a new policy from a later date"
The policy content is locked while a version uses it.
Create a new SLA policy and use it in a new service version.
"Service hours need at least one working day" or end before start
No day is ticked, or the End time is not after the Start time.
Tick the service days and set a later End time.
An agent is missing from the Agent list
They are inactive, lack servicedesk.agent, the employee is outside their scope, or it is their own request.
Check their role and data access scope; restricted cases also need servicedesk.confidential.
"Someone else has already taken this case."
Another agent clicked Take it first.
Refresh the request; reassign with More › Assign if needed.
Reply refused: "reopen it to continue the conversation"
The request is closed or cancelled.
Use More › Reopen with a reason (closed requests only), then reply.
Resolve refused: "This category needs the root cause (RCA)"
The category makes the root cause mandatory.
Fill in Root cause analysis (and a Root cause code) in the Resolve form.
Service analytics shows "Fewer than 5 employees raised requests in this period"
Figures are hidden to protect privacy.
Widen the From and To dates.
A grievance case is not in Cases
Its category is confidential with handler roles you do not hold, and you are not assigned or granted.
Ask the handler to grant you access with a reason.
Article edit shows "This page is not available to you"
Only drafts can be edited.
Click Start a revision on the article, then Edit.
An employee cannot find an article
It is not published, is archived, or the audience conditions exclude them.
Check Status and the Audience conditions; publish or widen the audience.

M21.intro: Communication and engagement is where you speak to your people and listen to them: announcements, notification rules, surveys, recognition, events, fundraisers, mission and values and the happiness index. Everything is prepared, approved by a second person where it matters, published to an audience and then measured.
M21.why: Without it, policies reach people by chance, nobody can prove who read or acknowledged them, and you have no safe, privacy-protected way to hear how people feel.
M21.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold every key. HR Manager prepares and approves announcements, surveys, campaigns, events and recognition. Managers and employees read announcements, take surveys, give badges and pledge. Auditors can view.
M21.where: Communication › Messaging (Announcements, Delivery log, Notification rules, Notification templates); Communication › Engagement (Engage desk, Audiences, Surveys, Campaigns, Events, Badges, Recognition, Reward points, Mission & values, Mood reasons, Happiness index, Feedback inbox); Communication › Fundraisers. Switches: Admin › Setup › Setup › Engage.
objectives: Prepare, approve, publish and track an announcement to a defined audience, with acknowledgement where needed.
Run a survey, campaign or event from draft to results while respecting anonymity and the privacy thresholds.
Set up recognition, reward points, mission and values, the mood bot and fundraisers, and read their results.

Users and roles: only employees with a sign-in account receive in-app and email messages
M20 Knowledge: announcements can link a published knowledge article; campaigns can include articles and HR services
M20 Helpdesk and grievances: feedback can be referred to the HR service desk or as an anonymous grievance
Letters: badge certificates use a letter template of type Badge certificate or Appreciation
Payroll: reward point redemptions and (when allowed) fundraiser pledges are paid or deducted in payroll

procedures.title: Create a saved audience
procedures.before: Know which companies, locations, departments or grades the group covers.
steps: Go to Communication › Engagement › Audiences and click New audience.
In the Audience step enter Code, Name and a Description.
In Audience criteria fill only the dimensions you need. Each filled dimension must match; values within one are alternatives.
Check the Review step and create. The audience is Active.
On the list click Count: you see how many employees match today inside your scope.
procedures.result: A reusable audience you can choose on announcements, surveys, events and fundraisers.

procedures.title: Prepare and submit an announcement
procedures.before: The text is final; any policy article is published; an audience exists or you know the criteria.
steps: Open Communication › Messaging › Announcements and click Compose.
Enter Title, Type, Body and Priority. Add Link a knowledge article, Publish at, Expires at or an Attachment (private) if needed.
In Audience & options turn on Employees must acknowledge if readers must confirm; choose a Saved audience or leave it empty.
Without a saved audience, fill Audience criteria. Empty means everyone employed in your scope.
Review and create. The announcement is listed as Draft.
In the row Actions choose Submit for approval and confirm. The message and audience are now frozen.
procedures.result: The announcement is In review, waiting for a second person to approve it.

procedures.title: Approve, publish and follow an announcement
procedures.before: A second person with communication.approve; you cannot approve your own announcement.
steps: The approver opens Announcements, chooses Actions › Approve and may add a note. Return to draft needs a note.
Choose Actions › Publish and confirm. With a future Publish at it becomes Scheduled; otherwise it publishes now.
On publishing the audience is fixed and delivery starts by In-app and Email.
Read SENT / FAILED / READ / ACK, e.g. 3 / 0 / 2 / 1 of 5 (illustrative). Check failures in the Delivery log.
Use New version for a correction. When it is published, the old version is archived.
Use Archive when the message is no longer current.
procedures.result: Employees have the announcement in their feed and acknowledgements are recorded and audited.

procedures.title: Check and resend a failed notification
procedures.before: Someone reports a missing message.
steps: Go to Communication › Messaging › Delivery log.
Use Status = Failed and, if needed, Channel = Email. Search for the person in To.
Click View to read Subject, Body and the Error.
For email, make sure the person has a correct email address on their user account.
Click Send again, give a Reason (at least 5 characters) and confirm. It is sent once and audited.
procedures.result: The message is sent again and the delivery shows Sent again.

procedures.title: Change who is told about an event
procedures.before: An existing rule and template for the event.
steps: Go to Notification rules, filter by Event and click Edit on the rule.
In Who is told, and how add or remove Audience rows: subject, line manager, a role or a user.
Tick In-app and Email. Do not rely on SMS, WhatsApp or Push: they are not connected.
Optionally add Only when rows, e.g. employee.department equals Sales.
Enter Reason for change and save. The change is audited.
procedures.result: The next matching event notifies the new audience.

procedures.title: Build and launch a survey
procedures.before: Know the questions, who should answer and how private answers must be.
steps: Open Surveys, click New survey, fill Code, Name, Survey type and Category, then Anonymity mode and Closes at.
On the survey, in Versions, open the draft's menu › Questions. Add each question with a key, type and prompt; save.
Choose Edit settings: response rule, results breakdown, Results visible to, reminders and the audience.
Choose Submit for approval. Content, audience and privacy are frozen.
A second person with engagement.approve chooses Approve.
Choose Publish. On the opening date the audience is fixed and invitations are sent; reminders follow.
procedures.result: The survey version is Open and employees can respond until it closes.

procedures.title: Read survey results safely
procedures.before: The version is open (identified) or closed (anonymous or confidential).
steps: On the survey, in Versions, click Results.
With fewer than 5 responses results are suppressed. Groups below the threshold are merged or hidden.
Free-text comments appear only overall and only with at least 10 answers.
Use Close now to stop responses early; anonymous and confidential results appear after closing.
procedures.result: Aggregate results you can share without exposing individuals.

procedures.title: Handle employee feedback
procedures.before: engagement.feedback; for referral to the service desk also servicedesk.agent.
steps: Go to Communication › Engagement › Feedback inbox and filter Status = New.
Click Read to see the feedback.
Choose Mark in review while you work on it.
Identified or confidential: Refer to HR service desk with a category (confidential needs an audited reason). Anonymous: Refer as anonymous grievance.
Otherwise choose Close and write a Handling note.
procedures.result: Each item is closed or referred, with a record of how it was handled.

procedures.title: Run an engagement campaign
procedures.before: The surveys, announcements, articles or services exist.
steps: Open Campaigns, click New engagement campaign, enter Code, Name, Starts on and Purpose.
Click Manage and use Add item to add each Survey, Announcement, Knowledge Base article or HR service.
Submit for approval; a second person approves.
Choose Schedule. On the start date each approved item is published by its own module.
Use Metrics to see recipients, sent, acknowledged and survey responses.
procedures.result: A campaign that launches its approved items together and reports on them.

procedures.title: Set up badges and recognition
procedures.before: Decide the monthly badge quota and whether custom badges are allowed (Admin › Setup › Setup › Engage).
steps: Open Badges. Nine standard badges exist; use Do not allow for any you do not want.
Click Add custom badge: name, code, icon, colour, description and core value.
Choose who may give and receive it, Public or Private, receiving limit, reason or attachment required, certificate.
Optionally link reward points (only used while reward points are on).
Colleagues use Give a badge on Recognition. You can Withdraw one with a reason.
procedures.result: Badges that match your culture and rules, given and tracked in Recognition.

procedures.title: Switch on and fund reward points
procedures.before: Agree a budget, a points policy and whether points can be redeemed through payroll.
steps: In Admin › Setup › Setup › Engage turn on Use reward points; set the point value and currency if points will be redeemed.
Publish a reward points policy that sets the credit cycle and points per cycle.
Open Reward points and click Deposit points to fund the budget.
Use Adjust points with a reason to correct a balance (negative takes points away).
Use Redeem for an employee; the amount is paid with the next payroll as a taxable earning.
procedures.result: A funded points budget and a ledger of every movement.

procedures.title: Publish an event and record attendance
procedures.before: A host and an audience; feedback templates if you want feedback.
steps: Open Events and click Add event. Fill Basics: name, type, host, mandatory or seats.
Enter Start date, Start time, Duration and any Repeat.
Choose Meeting location; add location and venue, or a Meeting URL for online.
Choose a Saved audience, paste employee codes, or criteria. Keep Publish when created on to invite now.
Open the event to see Invited, Not answered, Accepted, Declined and Seats left.
In the sessions list use Mark attendance; then Download attendance for a CSV.
procedures.result: Invitees are told, RSVPs tracked and attendance recorded per session.

procedures.title: Run a fundraiser
procedures.before: A cause, a target, dates and who may donate.
steps: Open Communication › Fundraisers and click Start a fundraiser.
Enter Campaign name, Purpose, Beneficiary and an optional document.
Enter Start date, End date, Target amount and Currency (e.g. INR).
Choose a saved audience or criteria; empty means everyone employed in your scope.
On Review turn on Open it now, or open it later. Employees see it on Home and pledge.
Record payment for each pledge paid outside payroll; Close when finished.
procedures.result: Collected against target, pledges and payments recorded.

procedures.title: Publish mission and values and start the mood bot
procedures.before: Agreed mission, vision and core values.
steps: Open Mission & values, click Add policy, enter Policy name, Code, Mission, Vision and Purpose.
In Advance details add each core value and keep Show on employees' Home on.
Leave Applies to empty for everyone; set In force from and Status Active.
Open Mood reasons; keep at most 20 active and use Preview to see the question.
In Admin › Setup › Setup › Engage turn on Enable mood bot? and set Frequency and Privacy control.
After each period ends, open Happiness index.
procedures.result: Values on Home and a privacy-safe mood measure.

procedures.title: Plan the engagement year from the Engage desk
procedures.before: None.
steps: Go to Communication › Engagement › Engage desk.
Read the top band; Nothing waiting means no register needs action.
Go down the areas: HR handbook, Announcement, Events, Survey, Recognition, Listening, Fundraiser.
Use Reports for ready-made badge, points and happiness reports.
Use Engage setup for switches, Mission & values and Mood reasons.
procedures.result: You know where each engagement activity lives and what needs attention.

calculations.title: Fundraiser progress
calculations.intro: Progress counts money collected plus pledges still to collect against the target, rounded down, never above 100%. Illustrative figures.
explain: Progress % = round down((collected + pledged) × 100 ÷ target), maximum 100.
Fundraiser view: Collected against target, Progress.

calculations.title: Reward points redemption amount
calculations.intro: When points are redeemed through payroll, the amount is fixed at the time of redemption. Illustrative figures: reward points are off in the example organisation.
lines: Value of one point (set in Setup › Engage)
total: Amount paid with the next payroll
explain: Amount = points × value per point, rounded to 2 decimals.
As a taxable earning with the next payroll.
Points on, payroll redemption chosen, a point value set, and its currency the same as payroll's.

calculations.title: Happiness index for one period
calculations.intro: Each check-in is a mood from 1 (Very unhappy) to 5 (Very happy). Illustrative period with 10 check-ins.
explain: A period or group with fewer than 5 check-ins shows no figures.

warnings.title: Only In-app and Email really send
warnings.headline: SMS, WhatsApp and Push are not connected today.
warnings.body: Notification rules offer SMS, WhatsApp and Push, but these channels only write a line to the server log. The Delivery log may still show them as Sent.
points: Choose In-app and Email on every rule.
Announcements always use In-app and Email only.
Email depends on each user having a correct email address.
warnings.todo: Remove SMS, WhatsApp and Push from your rules until PeopleOS support confirms a provider is connected.

warnings.title: A second person must approve
warnings.headline: You cannot approve your own announcement, survey or campaign.
warnings.body: Announcements, survey versions and campaigns need approval by someone other than the preparer. With only one administrator, nothing can be published.
points: Give communication.approve and engagement.approve to a second trusted person.
The approver must cover the whole audience in their data access.
warnings.todo: Name a second approver before your first announcement.

warnings.title: People without a sign-in account get nothing
warnings.headline: Recipients without a user account are skipped.
warnings.body: Announcements reach employees through their user account. In the example organisation both published announcements were skipped for all 5 recipients for this reason.
points: Invite employees as users before you publish.
Skipped people are not counted as sent or failed.
warnings.todo: Check that your audience has user accounts before publishing important messages.

warnings.title: Survey privacy cannot be undone
warnings.headline: Anonymous answers can never be linked to a person.
warnings.body: The privacy mode is fixed per version once submitted. Results of anonymous and confidential surveys appear only after the survey closes, and only above the thresholds.
points: At least 5 responses for any figure; at least 10 for free-text comments.
Identifying a confidential author needs a reason and is audited.
warnings.todo: Choose the privacy mode carefully and tell employees which one applies.

warnings.title: Published items are frozen
warnings.headline: Submitted announcements, survey versions and published events cannot be edited.
warnings.body: Submitting freezes content and audience. Corrections are made with New version (announcements, surveys); a published event's schedule is fixed.
points: The announcement edit screen shows "This page is not available to you" once it is not a draft.
To change a published event's time, cancel it and add a new event.
warnings.todo: Proof-read and check the audience before you submit.

warnings.title: Points value is a one-time setting
warnings.headline: The worth of a point and its currency lock once points exist.
warnings.body: The value per point and currency are locked as soon as the points ledger has an entry. Redemptions are paid as a taxable earning with payroll.
points: Decide the value before your first deposit.
A redemption already carried by a payroll run cannot be cancelled.
warnings.todo: Agree the points value with Finance before switching reward points on.

M22.intro: Reports and analytics turns your PeopleOS data into answers: 231 ready-made reports, your own reports built step by step, dashboards for different audiences, and overview pages for leaders. Everything follows each viewer's own permissions and data access.
M22.why: Without it, people export raw lists and build spreadsheets by hand, figures differ from meeting to meeting, and personal data leaves the system without control.
M22.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold every analytics key. HR Manager views dashboards, builds, runs and exports reports. The Executive role opens dashboards, the Workforce Command Centre and Workforce Intelligence. Auditors can view dashboards.
M22.where: Insights › Analytics: Dashboards, Dashboard builder, Reports, Report library, People analytics, Workforce Command Centre, Workforce Intelligence.
objectives: Find the right ready-made report in the Report library, add it to your reports, run it and export it to CSV.
Build, share and schedule your own report with filters, grouping and calculated fields.
Set up dashboards and CXO views for the right audience, and read the overview pages correctly.
depends_on: M03 People: the employee master feeds almost every report and headcount figure
M10 Attendance and M11 Leave: processed attendance and approved leave feed time reports and absenteeism
M13 Payroll: only finalized payroll runs feed payroll reports, people cost and cost per head
Users and roles: report access follows each user's permissions and data access
M20 Helpdesk and M21 Engagement: ticket, survey, badge and happiness reports use their data

procedures.title: Use a ready-made report
procedures.before: Know the question, e.g. "Who joined last month?"
steps: Go to Insights › Analytics › Report library.
Type in Search, e.g. joiners, or scroll to the area (People).
Click Use next to New joiners last month. Keep or change the Report name.
Choose Only for one employee (optional) to run it for a single person.
Click Create and open. The results appear at once and the report is in your Reports.
procedures.result: A saved report you can rerun any time, export or schedule.

procedures.title: Build your own report
procedures.before: Know the dataset and the fields you need.
steps: Open Reports and click New report. Enter Name and Description.
Choose the Dataset (grouped by area) and tick the Fields to show.
Add rows, e.g. Joining date / this financial year. Use a,b,c for "is any of".
Optionally choose Group by and aggregations such as Count or Sum of Gross.
Optionally add a calculated field: key, label and formula, e.g. employer_cost / paid_days.
Pick Show as, Sort by and Direction; set a Row limit if needed. Review and create.
procedures.result: Your report runs live under each viewer's access.

procedures.title: Run and export a report
procedures.before: analytics.export or analytics.manage to export.
steps: In Reports click Run on the report.
Read the heading, e.g. GROUPED RESULTS · 5 TOTAL, and the chart if there is one.
Click Export CSV. The file downloads and opens in Excel.
Edit the report and open Runs to download the same export later.
procedures.result: A CSV with every matching row (up to 10,000), recorded in the audit trail.

procedures.title: Schedule a report
procedures.before: You own the report; recipients are active users.
steps: In Reports click Edit and open the Schedules tab.
Click Add schedule and choose Frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) and the day.
Enter Time in 24-hour server time, e.g. 07:00.
Choose Recipients and keep Status Active.
After the first run, see Last run and the new line in Runs.
procedures.result: The report is exported on schedule and recipients get an in-app notice.

procedures.title: Share a report with colleagues
procedures.before: analytics.manage.
steps: In the Report step turn on Shared with everyone who can see the dataset.
Colleagues find it in Reports; each sees only the rows and fields they may see.
procedures.result: A shared report, also usable in dashboard widgets.

procedures.title: Read the dashboard
procedures.before: analytics.view.
steps: Headcount, Attrition (12 mo), Absenteeism (30 d) and People cost show the formula under the figure.
Use Open report under a chart or table widget.
Use Needs attention counts to go to exits or open tickets.
Use Switch dashboard when you have more than one.
procedures.result: You know the current state and where to look further.

procedures.title: Build a dashboard for an audience
procedures.before: Shared reports for the charts you want.
steps: Open Dashboard builder and click New dashboard. Enter Name, Visible to roles and Status.
Optionally set Applicable on and Values, named viewers and the payroll refresh day.
Optionally choose Recipients and Send (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) and the time.
Add widgets: type, title, metric or report, and size. Turn on Hide groups below the privacy threshold.
Check and create, then click Open to see it.
procedures.result: A dashboard listed for its audience, each viewer seeing figures under their own access.

procedures.title: Add a ready-made CXO view
procedures.before: analytics.manage.
steps: In Dashboard builder click Add a CXO view and pick a View, e.g. Employee movement.
Optionally enter a Name; the view is shared only with you at first.
On the edit screen choose roles or named people and Applicable on.
Set recipients and frequency; use Send now from the list to send the link at once.
procedures.result: A leadership view with the right audience and organisation slice.

procedures.title: Prepare a leadership briefing
procedures.before: analytics.executive.
steps: Open Workforce Command Centre and read MOVEMENT against last month.
Note headcount, tenure, attrition and absenteeism.
Read EXCEPTIONS and REQUIRES A DECISION; clear your approvals.
Open People analytics with As of set to the meeting date.
Use GO DEEPER › Reports to export the supporting lists.
procedures.result: A factual briefing with the reports behind each figure.

Payroll figures use only finalized payroll.
